issues.description: The specification/UML requires Farm.animals to be a List<Animal> implemented via ArrayList, but the solution implements it as a Set<Animal> using HashSet. This changes the required data structure semantics (ordering, duplicates) and contradicts the stated design students are asked to implement.
issues.suggestedFix: Change the solution Farm to use `private List<Animal> animals = new ArrayList<>();` with corresponding getter/setter signatures, imports, and iteration, aligning with the UML and problem statement.

issues.description: The template Farm.singFarmSongVerse method is stubbed without an Animal parameter (commented out), while the specification and solution define it as singFarmSongVerse(Animal animal). This mismatch can confuse students about the intended signature and how singFarmSong should call the helper.
issues.suggestedFix: Update the template signature to `private void singFarmSongVerse(Animal animal)` (and add the Animal import/class as needed) to match the UML/spec and allow singFarmSong() to call it directly.

issues.description: The Farm's animal collection type is inconsistent across artifacts: the problem statement/UML specifies an attribute named "animals" of type List<Animal> implemented with an ArrayList, but the provided solution implements it as Set<Animal> backed by a HashSet. This creates a conceptual mapping barrier for students because the required identifier/type combination (List/ArrayList) does not match the reference implementation (Set/HashSet), and it also affects expectations about ordering and duplicates when singing/feeding.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the solution (and expected design) with the specification by changing Farm.animals to List<Animal> and initializing with new ArrayList<>(), and update getter/setter/addAnimal/loops accordingly; alternatively, if Set is intended, update the problem statement/UML text to say Set<Animal> (HashSet) instead of List (ArrayList).

issues.description: The template's Farm.singFarmSongVerse method signature is commented out as "private void singFarmSongVerse(/*Animal animal*/)", while the problem statement and solution use "singFarmSongVerse(animal: Animal)" and "private void singFarmSongVerse(Animal animal)". This mismatch can confuse students about the required parameter identifier/type for the helper method when implementing singFarmSong().
issues.suggestedFix: Update the template stub to the correct signature: "private void singFarmSongVerse(Animal animal)" (and ensure Animal.java exists in the template), matching the problem statement and reference solution.
